aggregate_findings.interpretation: The App fixture cut adds two candidate affected fixture targets on the two historical pairs with broad App changes, but changes no required runnable test label in any of these four replayed pairs.
aggregate_findings.runtime_owning_suites: test_bridge and test_history_gateway were present in both arms for #15445 and #15713; absent from both arms for #15379 and #15255.

limitations: This is four selector-only historical pairs, not the 30-pair cohort qualification, and not a replay of the latest architecture source.
No tests or builds ran, so equal selected test labels do not establish behavioral equivalence or test pass status.
No timing or CI-saving claim is supported by these selector queries.
The original historical required-gate outcomes recorded per pair are context only and must not be confused with this successful selector-only replay.
The original query invocation UUIDs are not present in the archived payload; the outer BuildBuddy invocation and non-ID per-pair run names are recorded.

method.candidate_overlay_scope: Only the 11 App fixture ownership-cut paths listed in each pair record. The same pair-era compatibility adaptations were applied in both arms to keep old production pairs materializable.
method.expected_materialization_probe_exits: Observed nonzero exits are guarded git merge-file overlay-hunk probes and git show checks for fixture files absent in the old source pair. The exact guarded BUILD hunk was resolved as recorded; all final selector queries succeeded and result.errors is empty.
method.omitted_large_materialization_data: Four Git archive command stdout payloads per pair were omitted after preserving each archive SHA/size and validated tree ID. Selector/query outputs and hashes remain in the CAS evidence archive.
method.production_inputs: Each arm starts from the same pinned historical tested base and the exact CI synthetic tested-merge tree for that PR. The PR head commit is retained only as identity metadata and is not used as the merge input.
method.shared_state_and_cache_limit: The normal shared remote cache remained enabled and was not cleared or isolated; these were sequential selector queries in distinct source workspaces, with each queried Bazel server shut down. No cold/warm cache or execution-time comparison was measured.
